newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu defends suspension of general from talks.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu defends suspension of general from talks.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Sunday rejected criticism of his suspension from peace talks of an army general who met opposition leaders behind the government's back.
The Defence Ministry on Friday suspended Major-General Oren Shahor as head of the Israeli team in talks on civilian issues with the Palestinians until an investigation is completed.
In his first public comment on the affair, Netanyahu said: "We are talking about an officer -- I think this is a unique situation -- who was making contacts with the heads of parties secretly."
In the remarks broadcast by Israel Radio, Netanyahu said Shahor had failed to report to "those authorised" at a time of sensitive negotiations when protecting information was vital to their success.

Netanyahu said the parliamentary opposition, which reacted harshly to the suspension, had a right to be updated by himself or via other suitable channels. "But here we have a different situation," he said.

Shahor drew political fire after an Israeli newspaper published a photo on Thursday showing him leaving the home of former Labour Prime Minister Shimon Peres and said he also had met former Labour cabinet minister Yossi Beilin.
The officer had been a peace negotiator under Peres.

Israeli and Palestinian negotiators discussing civilian issues related to implementing Israel's long-delayed troop withdrawal from the West Bank town of Hebron have said they have nearly wrapped up a deal.
The sides still differ over security arrangements in the town, home to 100,000 Arabs and 400 Jews.
